query: For MnNiSi-based magnetic-refrigeration materials, what single intervention could improve mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected changes relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Isostructural alloying of MnNiSi with CoNiGe can improve mechanical performance while retaining a large magnetocaloric effect.
generation.conditions: The structural transition temperature (Tm) occurs within the Curie temperature window (CTW)
generation.mechanism: The introduction of CoNiGe stabilizes the Ni2In structure and lowers Tm, allowing for a large magnetic entropy change and a large conventional magnetocaloric effect
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved mechanical performance and retention of a large magnetocaloric effect
generation.boundary: The CTW is broad enough to allow for a large temperature range for the magnetoresponsive effects
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of the magnetostructural coupling and the optimal composition of the alloy are uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the magnetocaloric effect and mechanical performance of MnNiSi-based alloys with varying CoNiGe content
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the magnetocaloric effect decreases or the mechanical performance worsens with increasing CoNiGe content, the hypothesis is falsified

In order to obtain magnetostructural coupling, it is essential that the structural transition temperature (T m) occurs within the Curie temperature window (CTW)—the temperature range that spans between the magnetic Curie temperature (Tc) of the orthorhombic and hexagonal phases as depicted Figure 1a. It is known that, in MnM′X compounds, the stability of Ni2In and TiNiSi structures is highly dependent on the covalent bonds between M′ and X atoms, and that between the neighbouring Mn and Mn atoms. The stoichiometric tuning, foreign-atoms-substituting and applied stress may alter the strength of covalent bonds, thus influence Tt. For example, by introducing interstitial B atoms or substituting Cu for Mn atoms, Tt of MnCoGe can be reduced from 420 K to below Curie temperature of the orthorhombic phase (TC) and MST from PM hexagonal to FM orthorhombic phase is realized during cooling. In the case of MnNiGe system, the stoichiometric tuning can reduce Tt from 470 K to below than 200 K and obtain MST from FM hexagonal to AFM orthorhombic phase with decreasing temperature. em, Tt is successfully tuned down to below than TC, and the tunable MST between PM hexagonal and FM orthorhombic phase can be obtained in a large CTW by altering the CoNiGe-content. Due to the large ΔM between two phases, the observed MST can be induced by the external magnetic field at room temperature (RT). The effect is accompanied by a large magnetocaloric effect, indicating the potential applications in magnetic cooling refrigerator.
## Structural characterization
Figure 1(a) shows X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of (MnNiSi)1−x(CoNiGe)x (x = 0.32, 0.33, 0.34, 0.35, 0.36, 0.37, 0.38, 0.39, 0.40, 0.41, 0.42, 0.43 and 0.44) alloys measured at RT. It is reported that the stoichiometric MnNiSi exhibits the orthorhombic TiNiSi structure at RT, while CoNiGe possesses the stable hexagonal Ni2In structure. With the increase of CoNiGe-content, the structure of (MnNiSi)1−x(CoNiGe)x samples at RT changes from the orthorhombic TiNiSi to hexagonal Ni2In phase and no other impurity phase is found.
